en.S0-01: On Halloween night, a little turnip lantern lit up. It has a two-thousand-year story to tell.
en.S1-01: My story begins with a bonfire, two thousand years ago.
en.S1-02: Back then in Ireland, the Celts had just gathered the last sheaf of wheat.
en.S1-03: They celebrated Samhain, lighting bonfires to welcome the winter.
en.S1-04: The fire is so warm! Winter is coming!
en.S1-05: They say tonight, the door between two worlds grows thin!
en.S2-01: Legend says that on this night, mischievous spirits slip into our world.
en.S2-03: Put on your masks, so the spirits think we're one of them!
en.S2-04: I'm a little deer! Shh, don't laugh.
en.S2-05: And that's how Halloween costumes began.
en.S3-01: Many years later, November 1st became All Saints' Day.
en.S3-02: Dong, dong. Light a candle, and remember someone dear.
en.S3-03: The night before was called All Hallows' Eve.
en.S3-04: Say it fast enough, and it becomes Halloween!
en.S4-01: The Irish also loved telling the tale of Stingy Jack.
en.S4-02: Let me down! I promise I won't bother you anymore!
en.S4-03: Heh heh, a promise is a promise.
en.S4-04: Jack had nowhere to go, so he wandered the night with a turnip lantern.
en.S5-01: Later, on Halloween night, children went singing from door to door.
en.S5-02: Knock knock, we've come to sing!
en.S5-03: Here you go, warm soul cakes.
en.S5-04: Wuwu, shine a little brighter! On to the next house!
en.S5-05: In Scotland, children also dressed up and performed for treats.
en.S6-01: Later still, many Irish people sailed far away to America.
en.S6-02: Look, our new home! The pumpkins are huge!
en.S6-03: No turnips here? Then... catch my flame!
en.S6-05: And that's how the jack-o'-lantern was born.
en.S7-01: Today, every October 31st, kids dress up as witches, ghosts and kittens.
en.S7-03: Two thousand years... that's a long time.
en.S7-04: So every lantern lights the way home.
en.S7-05: Happy Halloween! Tonight, save a candy for the little guests at your door.
